title: HIV Treatment Adherence Challenges in Postpartum Women Living with HIV in the OPPTIM Study, Johannesburg, South Africa
content: Antiretroviral treatment (ART) adherence and viral load suppression (VLS) remains challenging postpartum for women living with HIV (WLHIV) globally and in South Africa (SA). The OPPTIM study evaluated ART adherence and VLS in postpartum WLHIV. We enrolled postpartum WLHIV and randomized them to arm 1 (standard-of-care VL 6-monthly) or arm 2 (point-of-care VL 3- monthly), with follow-up through 24-months (July 2018–March 2021). We administered sociodemographic and adherence questionnaires at each visit. We compared VLS rates (<50 copies/ml and <1000 copies/ml) to self-reported adherence. Logistic regression models were used to examine risk factors for sub-optimal adherence. Among the total sample of 405 postpartum women, 47.2% (191) reported sub-optimal HIV treatment adherence. Being born in Zimbabwe (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) 0.65 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.43-0.97) and mixed feeding (aOR 0.58 (95% CI 0.41-0.82)) was protective, while third trimester booking (aOR 2.15 (95% CI 1.03-4.47)) increased risks of sub-optimal adherence. In participants who self-reported ≥95% adherence, 6.0% (80/1325) had a VL ≥ 1000 copies/ml and 35.8% (475/1325) a VL ≥50 copies/ml. In conclusion our study identified adherence challenges among postpartum WLHIV in Johannesburg, SA. Strengthening adherence support may help reduce the risk of vertical HIV transmission.
